relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: Joab devastates Ammon and destroys Rabbah while David remains in Jerusalem—the same season in which Chronicles leaves Bathsheba and Uriah unspoken.
A conquered crown and immense spoil become David's public glory.
Rabbah's people are subjected to tools that may signify forced labor or lethal cruelty; neither reading permits triumphal silence.
War shifts to Gezer, where Sibbecai kills a Philistine champion.
Elhanan kills Lahmi in a tradition textually entangled with Goliath.
A man with polydactyly and great stature is turned into another champion story, though his body is simply human variation.
Jonathan kills him after his taunt.
The archive credits David's house with defeating the champions of Gath.

contemplative_note: Chronicles can omit a survivor and still preserve the campaign that endangered her. Silence is not innocence. Rabbah's ruined people, Bathsheba, Uriah, forced laborers, and opponents whose bodies are made strange all ask the reader to resist a heroic history built by editing out those harmed.
